newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian radio station cheers up troubled Mir crew.
newsitem.headline: Russian radio station cheers up troubled Mir crew.

text.p: A Russian radio station has brought some welcome light relief to the long-suffering cosmonauts on board the troubled space station Mir.

The programming director of Russkoye Radio, Stepan Stroyev, said on Tuesday that cosmonauts Vassily Tsibilyev and Alexei Lazutkin had been able to listen to music and answer questions sent in by listeners during a recent live radio link-up.

"We made this link-up (last Friday) with the help of Mission Control... because things are not looking too good up there. It's not the happiest time for them and we wanted to cheer them up," Stroyev told Reuters.

Later on Tuesday two new cosmonauts were due to blast off from the Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan to relieve Tsibilyev and Lazutkin, who have been facing problems with the oxygen-generating system on the 11-year-old space station.
The new cosmonauts will undertake difficult repairs on Mir, which was badly damaged in a collision on June 25 with a supply ship. The repairs will determine the space station's fate.
"We had (music) requests from the cosmonauts and their wives. There was a live communication link. You could hear the cosmonauts talk," Stroyev said.
"Listeners phoned in and sent their best wishes to the cosmonauts and people from Mission Control also took part," he added. The link-up lasted an hour.
The Moskovsky Komsomolyets newspaper said on Tuesday that the cosmonauts' wives requested a song for their husbands called "I will pray for you".
Stroyev said the radio had proposed to Mission Control making further link-ups with Mir lasting several hours with the cosmonauts acting as disc jockeys.
"It would be fun both for them and for listeners," he said, adding no time had been fixed because it was technically difficult to organise.
